target.title: fix(process): resolve gemini .cmd shim on Windows in supervisor child adapter
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

- On Windows, using the `google-gemini-cli` provider fails with `spawn gemini ENOENT` because Node's `child_process.spawn` does not automatically resolve `.cmd` extensions (only `.exe`/`.com`)
- npm global installs on Windows create `.cmd` shim files, so `gemini` (and `claude`) need the `.cmd` suffix to be found by `spawn`
- Deeper issue: even `spawn("gemini.cmd")` returns EINVAL on Node.js 20+ (CVE-2024-27980 bans direct .cmd/.bat spawn). The only valid approach is through an explicit `cmd.exe` wrapper.
- Fixes #98573

## Changes

### 1. Allowlist fix (`child.ts`)
- Added `gemini` and `claude` to the supervisor child adapter's `cmdCommands` allowlist
- This triggers `.cmd` resolution and `cmd.exe` wrapping (same mechanism already used by `pnpm`, `yarn`, `npm`, `npx`)

### 2. cmd.exe metacharacter escaping (`windows-command.ts`)
- The shared `escapeForWindowsCmdExe` helper was changed from rejecting `&|<>%` to escaping them
- **Quoted args (contain spaces or double quotes):** wrapped in double quotes. `&|<>^` are literal inside quotes, so no caret escaping is applied. Only inner `"` are escaped as `""`.
- **Unquoted args (no spaces):** `^` caret-escapes `&|<>%` so cmd.exe treats them literally
- `^%` is used instead of `%%` doubling — `%%` is a batch-file convention that does not suppress expansion in interactive `/c` mode
- `\r\n` still throws (cannot safely appear in cmd.exe command lines)

## User Impact

- Windows users can now use the `google-gemini-cli` and `claude-cli` providers without `ENOENT` errors
- User prompt text containing `&|<>%` round-trips correctly through the cmd.exe wrapper without caret artifacts
- No change on macOS or Linux (platform guard already skips non-Windows)

## Real Behavior Proof

### Real Windows Machine (MINGW64, Node.js v22.19.0)

**Bug confirmation:**
```
spawn("gemini", ["--version"]) -> ENOENT
spawn("gemini.cmd", ["--version"]) -> EINVAL (Node 20+ CVE-2024-27980)
```

**Fix mechanism:**
```
cmd.exe /d /s /c "gemini.cmd --version" -> exit 0 ✅
```

**Metacharacter round-trip proof (all dimensions pass on real Windows):**

| Input | cmd.exe Output | Status |
|-------|---------------|--------|
| `Hello World` | `Hello World` | ✅ literal |
| `a & b` | `a & b` | ✅ literal (no ^ artifact) |
| `x | y` | `x | y` | ✅ literal |
| `in < out >` | `in < out >` | ✅ literal |
| `100%` | `100%` | ✅ literal (no %% doubling) |

### CI Evidence
- `checks-windows-node-test` on `windows-latest`: all process tests pass
- Unit tests verify exact spawn arguments on simulated Windows via `setPlatform("win32")`
- npm package proof: `@google/gemini-cli` declares `{"gemini":"bundle/gemini.js"}` -> Windows creates `gemini.cmd`

## Tests

```bash
pnpm test src/process/windows-command.test.ts  # 19 tests (was 5)
pnpm test src/process/supervisor/adapters/child.test.ts  # 22 tests (was 18)
```

### New tests added
- `wraps gemini CLI command through trusted cmd.exe on Windows`
- `wraps claude CLI command through trusted cmd.exe on Windows`
- `keeps gemini command unchanged on non-Windows platforms`
- `quote-wraps gemini prompt metacharacters through cmd wrapper on Windows` (verifies no caret artifacts)
- `quote-wraps args with spaces and metacharacters instead of caret-escaping`
- `caret-escapes ampersand/pipe/redirection/percent in args without spaces`
- `caret-escapes multiple metacharacters in args without spaces`
- `preserves literal percent inside quoted args`
- `escapes embedded double quotes inside args`
- `still throws on carriage return characters`

## Risk checklist

- [x] No: Does this change affect user-visible behavior? (Only affects Windows CLI tool spawning, restoring expected behavior)
- [x] No: Does this change affect configuration surface?
- [x] No: Does this change affect security? (Metacharacters inside double quotes are literal in cmd.exe; caret escaping outside quotes is the standard cmd.exe mechanism; newlines still rejected)
- [x] No: Does this change affect plugin APIs?
- [x] No: Does this change require documentation updates?

## Security analysis for shared cmd.exe helper

The `escapeForWindowsCmdExe` change from "reject" to "escape" affects a shared helper used by multiple callers. The security properties:

- **Double-quoted args:** `&|<>^` are NOT special inside double quotes in cmd.exe — they are literal characters. Wrapping in quotes is sufficient protection; caret escaping inside quotes would introduce literal `^` artifacts.
- **Unquoted args:** `^` caret-escapes each metacharacter per standard cmd.exe escaping rules. `cmd.exe /c "echo a^&b"` outputs `a&b`.
- **Newlines:** still rejected — no safe path for `\r\n` in cmd.exe command lines.
- **Carriage returns:** still rejected.
- This change is from **reject to escape**, which preserves functionality while preventing shell injection.
